questions.q: How has the European Union emerged as an alternative centre of power?
answer: After the Second World War, the countries of Western Europe came together for economic cooperation, and this steadily grew into the European Union, an important alternative centre of power.

answer.text: Beginning as the European Economic Community, the process culminated in the Maastricht Treaty of 1992, which created the European Union. It developed a single market, a common currency called the Euro, and its own flag, anthem and parliament, uniting many nations into one bloc.

The EU is an economic giant, one of the world's largest trading powers, with a combined economy rivalling the United States. It also has political and diplomatic influence, with two of its members holding permanent seats in the UN Security Council, and it possesses considerable military strength.
However, member states guard their sovereignty, and differences among them limit a common foreign policy, as seen when some opposed EU decisions.

answer: Thus the EU stands as a major economic and political power, offering a counterweight to US dominance.

questions.q: How has China emerged as a major centre of power in world politics?

answer.text: has risen to become a major power chiefly through its remarkable economic growth over recent decades.

list: From the late 1970s it opened its economy with reforms, attracting foreign investment and technology
It became the 'factory of the world', with huge exports and rapid growth
Its large economy gives it great weight in world trade and finance
It has built up its military and expanded its influence in Asia, Africa and beyond, making it a rising challenger to US dominance

questions.q: What have been the achievements and limitations of ASEAN as a regional organisation?

answer.text: the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, has become an important regional organisation with notable achievements and some limitations.

list: It has promoted peace and stability in a once war-torn region and settled disputes through dialogue
It has built economic cooperation and a free trade area, boosting trade and growth
Its members differ in size, wealth and political systems, making common action hard
It follows a policy of non-interference and consensus, which can slow decisions on difficult issues
